vocab.definition: transfers energy to the surroundings (gets hotter).
takes in energy from the surroundings (gets colder).
everything around the reaction (e.g. the water).

misconceptions.right: Energy is taken in, not destroyed.

infoPanels.title: ENDOTHERMIC PROFILE
infoPanels.secondaryContent: Products are higher than reactants — energy is taken in.

questions.text: State what is meant by an exothermic reaction. [1 mark]
Classify combustion and thermal decomposition as exo- or endothermic. [2 marks]
Explain why the temperature of the surroundings falls in an endothermic reaction. [2 marks]
Give a use of an exothermic and an endothermic change. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: An exothermic reaction ______ energy, so products are at a ______ energy level.

questions.text: A reaction profile shows products below reactants. State the type of reaction and why. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Exo = exit heat (hotter). Endo = energy in (colder).
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does an exothermic reaction have products at a lower energy than reactants?
